<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="Sp1nd01" /></noinclude>{{Verse|1|24}} Neuertheles, to abide in the felſh, {{smaller|is}} more needfull for you.

{{Verse|1|25}} And hauing this confidence, I know that I ſhall abide and continue with you all, for your furtherance and ioy of faith,

{{Verse|1|26}} That your reioycing may bee more abundant in Ieſus Chriſt for me, by my comming to you againe.

{{Verse|1|27}} Onely let your conuerſation bee as it becommeth the Goſpel of Chriſt, that whether I come and ſee you, or elſe be abſsent, I may heare of your affaires, that yee ſtand faſt in one ſpirit, with one minde, ſtriuing together for the faith of the Goſpel,

{{Verse|1|28}} And in nothing terrified by your aduerſaries, which is to them an euident token of perdition: but to you of ſaluation, and that of God.

{{Verse|1|29}} For vnto you it is giuen in the behalfe of Chriſt, not onely to beleeve on him, but alſo to ſuffer for his ſake,

{{Verse|1|30}} having the ſame conflict which ye ſaw in me, and now heare {{smaller|to be}} in me.

==={{Chapter|2|CHAP. II.}}===

{{smaller block|He exhorteth to vnitie, and to all humbleneſſe of minde, by example of Chriſts humilitie and exaltation: [[#2:12|12]] To a carefull proceeding in the way of ſaluation, that they bee as lights to the wicked world, [[#2:16|16]] and comforts to him their Apoſtle, who is now ready to bee offered vp to God. [[#2:19|19]] He hopeth to ſend Timothie to them, whom hee greatly commendeth, [[#2:25|25]] as Epaphroditus alſo, whom he preſently ſendeth to them.}}

{{Verse|2|1|notext=}}{{dropinitial|I|image=King James Bible (1611) page A2r (I).png|imgsize=100px}}F {{smaller|there bee}} therefore any conſolation in Chriſt, if any comfort of loue, if any fellowſhip of the Spirit, if any bowels, ⁊ mercies;

{{Verse|2|2}} Fulfill ye my ioy, that yee be like minded, hauing the ſame loue, being of one accord, of one minde.

{{Verse|2|3}} Let nothing bee {{smaller|done}} through ſtrife, or vaine glory, but in lowlineſſe of minde let each eſteeme other better then themſelues.

{{Verse|2|4}} Looke not euery man on his owne things, but euery man alſo on the things of others.

{{Verse|2|5}} Let this minde bee in you, which was alſo in Chriſt Ieſus:

{{Verse|2|6}} Who being in the forme of God, thought it not robbery to bee equall with God:

{{Verse|2|7}} But made himſelfe of no reputation, and tooke vpon him the forme of a ſeruant, and was made in the ǁ{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=ǁ ''Or, habite''}} likeneſſe of men.

{{Verse|2|8}} And being found in faſhion as a man, he humbled himſelfe, and became obedient vnto death, euen the death of the Croſſe.

{{Verse|2|9}} Wherefore God alſo hath highly exalted him, and giuen him a Name which is aboue euery name:

{{Verse|2|10}} That at the Name of Ieſus euery knee ſhould bow, of {{smaller|things}} in heauen, and {{smaller|things}} in earth, and {{smaller|things}} vnder the earth:

{{Verse|2|11}} And that euery tongue ſhould confeſſe, that Ieſus Chriſt is Lord, to the glory of God the Father.

{{Verse|2|12}} Wherefore, my beloued, as ye haue alwayes obeyed, not as in my preſence onely, but now much more in my abſence; worke out your owne ſaluation with feare, and trembling.

{{Verse|2|13}} For it is God which worketh in you, both to will, and to doe, of {{smaller|his}} good pleasure.

{{Verse|2|14}} Doe all things without murmurings, and diſputings: 

{{Verse|2|15}} That yee may bee blameleſſe and ǁ{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=ǁ ''Or, ſyncere.''}} harmeleſſe, the ſonnes of God, without rebuke, in the middes of a crooked and peruerſe nation, among whom ǁ{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=ǁ ''Or, ſhine ye''}} ye ſhine as lights in the world:

{{Verse|2|16}} Holding foorth the word of life, that I may reioyce in the day of Chriſt, that I have not runne in vaine, neither laboured in vanie.

{{Verse|2|17}} Yea, and if I bee †{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=† ''Gr, powred foorth.''}} offered vpon the ſacrifice and ſeruice of your faith, I ioy, and reioyce with you all.

{{Verse|2|18}} For the ſame cauſe alſo doe ye ioy, and reioyce with me. 

{{Verse|2|19}} ǁ{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=ǁ ''Or, moreouer.''}} But I truſt in the Lord Ieſus, to ſend Timotheus ſhortly vnto you, that I alſo may bee of good comfort, when I know your ſtate.

{{Verse|2|20}} For I haue no man ǁ{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=ǁ ''Or, ſo deare vnto mee.''}} like minded, who will naturally care for your ſtate.

{{Verse|2|21}} For all ſeeke their owne, not the things which are Ieſus Chriſts.

{{Verse|2|22}} But ye know the proofe of him, That as a ſonne with the father, hee hath ſerued with me, in the Goſpel.

{{Verse|2|23}} Him therefore I hope to ſend preſently, ſo ſoone as I ſhall ſee how it wil goe with me.

{{Verse|2|24}} But I truſt in the Lord, that I alſo my selfe ſhall come ſhortly.

{{Verse|2|25}} But I ſuppoſed it neceſſary, to ſend you Epaphroditus my brother and companion in labour, and fellow<noinclude></noinclude>
